title: Everybody's Golf
subtitle: A golf course becomes a place to spend time

body: Everybody's Golf is Clap Hanz and Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 sports game, first released in North America on 29 August 2017. The series' accessible shot-making returns inside courses that can be explored more freely, with a created golfer taking part in the wider setting. Players can walk around and drive golf carts instead of treating each hole only as the next isolated screen. That freedom gives the surroundings another role. A course is still a sequence of sporting problems, but it also becomes a place whose shape and routes can be encountered between shots.

The approachable presentation leaves room for attention to distance, terrain and the desired landing position. A successful shot depends on choosing an appropriate approach and carrying it out consistently, with later attempts making a familiar hole easier to judge. The player develops a personal golfer while encountering different conditions and challenges. Exploration gives another way to understand the layout, connecting the visible landscape to the decisions made during play. The game keeps the distinction between an easy-to-understand action and the longer process of learning where that action should send the ball.

The PlayStation 4 release followed years of Everybody's Golf games across Sony consoles and handhelds. Its character creation and open elements were presented as a new direction when the project was announced in 2014. Clap Hanz developed it with Japan Studio, maintaining the series' bright visual character and accessible entry point. Online play originally extended the social setting beyond the local course. Its particular contribution is the way it loosens the spaces between shots, allowing a traditionally structured sports game to include the less directed pleasure of simply being around the course with other people.
